Settings:

  • Row 1 is the header row; no title, no merged cells, no colours.
  • phone: Format → Number → Plain text, so +234 and every digit survive.
  • area: Data → Data validation → Dropdown (Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Dugbe, Agodi, Challenge) → Reject the input.
  • is_vip: Insert → Checkbox (TRUE/FALSE).

Tests: typing "Bodja" in area is rejected. Typing text such as "08012" or "₦8,012" into a column with a number rule is rejected (if your Customers tab has no number column yet, test it on a temporary column with "Is valid number").

Same-name check: CUST-0003 (Bodija) and CUST-0004 (Mokola) are both "Mrs Ade", but the IDs keep them apart.
mistakes: Phones typed as numbers, so the leading digits or the +234 disappear.
IDs without padding (CUST-1, CUST-10), which sort out of order.
Validation set to "Show a warning" instead of "Reject the input", so the Bodja test gets through.
VIP shown by highlighting the row instead of a checkbox column.
b.pass: Ten customers with padded CUST- IDs, two same-name customers with different IDs, phones as plain text in +234 form, an area dropdown that rejects "Bodja", a VIP checkbox, and all seven rules visibly met.
b.redo: Send it back for a title row or colour used as data, numeric phones, a dropdown that only warns, or same-name customers sharing an ID.

Worked example: five Harvest Lane orders. Prices: TOM-CRATE ₦12,500, TOM-CRATE-S ₦7,000, PEP-TATASHE-L ₦9,000, ONI-BAG ₦4,000. Delivery fee ₦1,500. Formulas are those from the solved problem, filled down.

HL-0043CUST-0007Mrs AdebayoDelivered3400035500
HL-0044CUST-0012Mrs AdePaid1200013500
HL-0045CUST-0015Mrs AdeNew → Delivered1250014000
HL-0046CUST-0019Mr OkaforOut for delivery1800019500
HL-0047CUST-0007Mrs AdebayoPaid2400025500

Order_Items has eight rows: two for HL-0043, one each for HL-0044, HL-0045 and HL-0046, and three for HL-0047 (TOM-CRATE-S × 1, ONI-BAG × 2, PEP-TATASHE-L × 1).

Hand check of HL-0047: 7,000 + (2 × 4,000) + 9,000 = 24,000 items, + 1,500 fee = 25,500. The formula total matches. HL-0043 totals 35,500, the same as the hand calculation in 0.3.

Lifetime spend test (=SUMIFS(Orders!I:I, Orders!C:C, A2, Orders!G:G, "Delivered")):

CustomerBeforeAfter HL-0045 set to Delivered
CUST-0007 Mrs Adebayo35500 (HL-0047 is only Paid)35500
CUST-0012 Mrs Ade, Bodija00
CUST-0015 Mrs Ade, Mokola014000

Only the Mokola Mrs Ade changed. That proves the ID, not the name, drives every link: a lookup by name would have credited the wrong Mrs Ade. No cell shows "Unknown customer" or "Unknown SKU".
mistakes: Looking up unit_price from Products with a formula, so old orders change when prices change.
Retyping IDs with a trailing space, which produces "Unknown customer".
Prices typed with ₦ or commas, so items_total comes out as 0.
lifetime_spend summing every order instead of Delivered only.
s.pass: Four linked tabs, five orders including a three-item order and one order for each same-name customer, HL-0043 totalling 35,500, no "Unknown" results, a written hand check that matches its formula total, and lifetime_spend changing only when an order becomes Delivered.
s.redo: Send it back if any total is typed rather than calculated, a formula shows Unknown or #REF!, or lifetime_spend counts orders that aren't Delivered.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane rebuilt in Airtable (same five orders as Silver).

  • Orders: Customer (link to Customers), Order items (link to Order_Items), delivery_fee (number), status (single select: New, Paid, Out for delivery, Delivered, Cancelled), items_total (rollup of line_total with SUM(values)), total (formula {items_total} + {delivery_fee}).
  • Order_Items: Order (link), Product (link), qty (number), unit_price (number, typed at sale), line_total (formula {qty} * {unit_price}).
  • Views: Orders kanban grouped by status; a form view for new orders.

Recommendation (sample). Give Tolu Google Sheets today. It's free, she already knows it, and every platform in this course connects to it. The cost is discipline: anyone can type over a formula, so the formula columns stay protected. Airtable was easier in two ways: linked records replaced every XLOOKUP, and the kanban gave riders a clear board. Its one trap: if unit_price is a lookup from Products, old orders change when prices change, so I kept it as a typed number. Switch trigger: move to Airtable when more than two people edit orders every day, or when Tolu wants a kanban board for riders. Check Airtable's current free-plan record limits before switching.

Submit: screenshots of both builds, the kanban and form views, the totals table and this recommendation.
mistakes: Making unit_price a lookup of the current product price, so Airtable totals drift away from Sheets.
Typing items_total by hand instead of using a rollup.
A recommendation like "switch when we grow" with no specific trigger.
Comparing only one order, so a mismatch elsewhere goes unnoticed.
g.pass: An Airtable base with the four linked tables, a rollup for items_total, a formula for total, a kanban by status and a form view; a table showing identical totals in both builds; and a recommendation that names a measurable switching trigger.
g.redo: Send it back if totals differ without explanation, the rollup or views are missing, or the recommendation has no concrete trigger.
